new.st: The Whiskey Hollow robbers examined their haul after riding the stolen engine and threw it away in a corn field: watches, cutlery and cheap jewelry from the express safe. The gang leader described the place in his deathbed statement to St. Louis police in October 1904. No recovery was reported. Pin is approximate, not the spot itself.

set.n: Whiskey Hollow hold-up of Rock Island No. 11, south of Muscatine
set.pl: Up-grade on the Rock Island (BCR&N) line between Muscatine and Fruitland, where it climbs out of the Mississippi bottoms (paper: train 'laboring up grade' entering Whiskey Hollow, 'darkness and dense woods'); spot on the grade not fixed
set.st: Five men stopped Rock Island train No. 11 at a bonfire in Whiskey Hollow, after the leader rode from Muscatine on a ticket to Fruitland and pulled the emergency brake. They blew the express safe with nitroglycerin, cut off the engine and ran it through Letts toward Columbus Junction. The railway said no money was taken; the dying leader later said they got only cheap jewelry, watches, knives and forks. The gang kept a tent camp across the Mississippi and came over by skiff. The forum's '1910' date is this 1904 robbery. Pin is approximate, not the spot itself.
set.t: History pin: the loot was thrown away elsewhere (see the corn-field pin SW of Columbus Junction). Old grade cuts south of Muscatine may show on LiDAR. Access: private.

set.n: Black diamonds lost in the 1929 mail-plane crash, SW of Harmon
set.pl: Sterling Daily Gazette: pilot landed about 6 mi SW of Harmon, plane crashed about 1 mi SE of where he landed; pin offset from Harmon by those distances, farm not yet on a plat
set.st: A National Air Transport mail plane (Curtiss Falcon) lost in fog jumped by its pilot on 22 March 1929 crashed and burned on a farm southwest of Harmon. It carried a shipment of black (industrial) diamonds from El Paso to New York worth over $30,000. Postal inspectors dug and sifted tons of swamp mud and ash and recovered about $25,000; in June 1929 twenty-nine stones worth about $5,000 were still being sought. The pilot was taken to Walnut. Pin is approximate, not the spot itself.
set.t: Green River lowland farm fields; landowner permission. A 1920s Lee County plat would give the section (owner names are in research/ia-il). Access: private.

set.n: Andy Dickson's buried gold, farm NW of Palmyra
set.pl: Des Moines Register 31 Oct 1909: farm 'about ten miles northeast of Indianola, and two miles northwest of Palmyra'; pin 2 mi NW of GNIS Palmyra, farm not yet on a plat
set.st: Andy Dickson, 80, died in August 1909 with no money in any bank. Digging around an old shed used as a smoke house, about twenty yards from the house, turned up $2,300 in gold, then two jars holding $10,005; by the end of October $13,300 in $20, $10, $5 and $1 gold pieces had been found. Officials believed more than $25,000 was buried. The night before he died he said he had 'lots and lots of money' and would have to show where it was. The house was a 1.5-story frame house on a rise over 100 ft back from the road, hidden in a grove of elm and maple, with 10-12 outbuildings. Pin is approximate, not the spot itself.
set.t: Find Dickson on a 1900s-1910s Warren County plat to fix the forty. About half the believed total was never reported found. Access: private: permission.

set.n: Reuben Bennett, the Hamilton County miser, farm 2 mi from Webster City
set.y: lived there c.1878-1898; died autumn 1898; searched to 1903
set.pl: Papers: 800-acre farm 'two miles from the city' (Webster City), next to the county poor farm; direction not given, pin at Webster City with a 3.5 km ring
set.st: Reuben Bennett, formerly of Portsmouth, Ohio, lived alone for about twenty years in a small hut on his 800-acre farm two miles from Webster City, refusing to sell hay or stock; the manager of the neighbouring poor farm found him dead in bed in autumn 1898. Relatives and a daughter from Helena fought over the estate, and in 1903 relatives were still searching for his buried thousands, which had not been found. Pin is approximate, not the spot itself.
set.t: Place Bennett's 800 acres and the Hamilton County poor farm on an 1890s-1900s plat. Buried money is in one paper only (1903), so C. Access: private.

set.n: $1,300 in gold plowed up, old Patrick Callahan farm near Lansing
set.st: In May 1921 farm hand John Brazell (Brassell) plowed up a glass fruit jar of gold coins, $2.50 to $20 pieces, about $1,300 in all, in a field on the old Patrick Callahan farm near Lansing; it had been buried for many years. One wire copy printed $19,300; the Iowa copies say $1,300. Pin is approximate, not the spot itself.

set.n: The Iwers brothers' hidden fortune, 880-acre farm near Sunbury
set.y: hidden to 1936; dug July 1936; $21,000 still sought
set.pl: AP: farm 'twelve miles east of' Tipton, '880-acre farm near Sunbury, ten miles east of here'; pin between due-east-of-Tipton and GNIS Sunbury, farm not yet on a plat
set.st: Bachelor brothers John, Henry and William Iwers hid their money on their 880-acre farm. After Henry, the last of them, died on 30 May 1936, an iron box with $112,000 in gold coin, gold and silver certificates and securities was dug from an old machine shed, after an earlier iron box with $88,000 in securities; more was hidden in the house. Over $212,000 was found in all against an estate put at $350,000, and in late July 1936 the court held the estate open for a search for $21,000 more. Guards were posted during the hunts. Pin is approximate, not the spot itself.
set.t: Place the Iwers 880 acres on a 1920s-30s Cedar County plat near Sunbury. Most was found; the July 1936 search for $21,000 more has no reported result. Access: private: permission.

set.n: Fisherman Andrew Mattson's $8,000 on the lake shore, South Chicago
set.pl: Washington Times 24 Dec 1905: his cabin stood on the Lake Michigan shore at the foot of 103rd Street; money said to be on the shore between Calumet Park and the Indiana line
set.st: Andrew Mattson, the 'hermit fisherman' of South Chicago, lived thirty years in a weather-beaten cabin on the lake shore at the foot of 103rd Street. Dying in December 1905 he told his wife of about $8,000 saved and hidden on the shore, then lost his speech. His widow kept watch on the cabin and hundreds searched; by January 1906 the money had not been found near the hut.
set.t: Lakefront is park and industry now: check rules. Access: city park/industrial: check.
